field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The swell came up today and there were not many boats fishing. There were a few sea bass caught in the same area. The wind did blow around noon.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast November 6, 2026 Eureka, Trinidad Crab Openers Delayed Due to Domoic Acid In press release issued on Nov. 6, CDFW has taken the recommendation of the CA Dept. of Public Health to delay the Dungeness crab season from he southern boundary of the Reading Rock State Marine Protected Areas (41⁰ 17.6’ N. latitude) to the southern boundary of the Ten Mile State Marine Reserve (39° 33.3’ N. latitude). This area includes Trinidad and Eureka. CDFW Statement: State health agencies have determined that Dungeness crab from the southern boundary of the Reading Rock State Marine Protected Areas (41⁰ 17.6’ N. latitude) to Cape Mendocino, Humboldt County (40⁰ 10’ N. latitude) pose a human health risk due to elevated levels of domoic acid and recommended a delay of the recreational Dungeness crab fishery. Following this recommendation, California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) Director Meghan Hertel has delayed the recreational Dungeness crab fishery in this area. field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: The marine forecast thru this weekend into the first part of next week looks very rough for the waters outside of Depoe Bay. Heavy winds and seas are forecasted thru the period so best bet is to keep in touch with the office at Dockside for any signs of a break in the forecast. It's the winter time and like always we go thru these periods and things will get better.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
